title: Being locally of finite type descends along fpqc coverings (Stacks 02KX)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering of $S$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. For $i\in I$ let $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ be the base change of $f$ along $g_i$, the second projection of the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f_i$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] for every $i\in I$, then $f$ is locally of finite type.

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KX (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type, line 5737: 'The property P(f) = "f is locally of finite type" is fpqc local on the base'), the direction 'each base change $X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ has the property $\Rightarrow$ $f$ has it' of 'fpqc local on the base', Descent, Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310)

proof.text: *Being locally of finite type is invariant under isomorphism and Zariski local on the base (conditions (0) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion] for $\mathcal P$ = locally of finite type).* By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] a morphism $f:X\to S$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] if and only if every $x\in X$ lies in an affine open $U\subseteq X$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ for an affine open $V\subseteq S$ such that $\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]; we use this form. (0): let $f:X\to S$ be locally of finite type and $a:X\to\tilde X$, $b:S\to\tilde S$ isomorphisms with $\tilde f\circ a=b\circ f$. For $\tilde x=a(x)\in\tilde X$ take $U\ni x$, $V$ as above for $f$. Then $a(U)\ni\tilde x$ and $b(V)$ are affine opens [def-pc-scheme] with $\tilde f(a(U))\subseteq b(V)$, and $\mathcal O_{\tilde S}(b(V))\to\mathcal O_{\tilde X}(a(U))$ is identified with $\mathcal O_S(V)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$ through the ring isomorphisms $b^\sharp,a^\sharp$, hence is of finite type (the images under $a^\sharp$ of finitely many generators generate); so $\tilde f$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion]. (2): let $S=\bigcup_kV_k$ be an open covering such that every restriction $f^{-1}(V_k)\to V_k$ is locally of finite type. For $x\in X$ pick $k$ with $f(x)\in V_k$; [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] for $f^{-1}(V_k)\to V_k$ gives affine opens $x\in U\subseteq f^{-1}(V_k)$, $V\subseteq V_k$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ and $\mathcal O(V)\to\mathcal O(U)$ of finite type. An affine open of an open subscheme is an affine open of the ambient scheme, with the same ring of sections [def-pc-scheme]; so the same $U,V$ serve for $f$ at $x$, and $f$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KX (lemma-descending-property-locally-finite-type, line 5737), proof, second sentence: 'Being locally of finite type is Zariski local on the base, see Morphisms, Lemma 01T2' (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, morphisms.tex line 2673); invariance under isomorphism is the convention of Definition Tag 02KO (definition-property-morphisms-local, line 5310)

proof.text: *Being locally of finite type is stable under base change (condition (1)).* If $f:X\to S$ is locally of finite type and $g:S'\to S$ is any morphism, in particular a flat one, then the second projection $X\times_SS'\to S'$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KX, proof, first sentence: 'Being locally of finite type is preserved under base change, see Morphisms, Lemma 01T4' (lemma-base-change-finite-type, morphisms.tex line 2732)

proof.text: *Condition (3), the ring map of the base.* Let $g:S'\to S$ be a flat surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] morphism of affine schemes, $f:X\to S$ a morphism, $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and assume $f'$ locally of finite type. By step 1 (invariance under isomorphism, applied to $f$, $g$ and $f'$) we may assume $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ [def-pc-scheme]; then $g=\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ for a unique ring map $\rho:R\to R'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $g$ is flat, $\rho$ is a flat ring map by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Since $g$ is surjective, the map of prime spectra $\mathfrak q\mapsto\rho^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, which is the map of underlying sets of $\operatorname{Spec}\rho$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], is surjective. Hence $\rho$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KX, proof: 'let S' -> S be a flat surjective morphism of affine schemes ... Write S = Spec(R), S' = Spec(R') ... We know that R -> R' is faithfully flat' (the faithful flatness is Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HQ, lemma-ff-rings, algebra.tex line 9164, with Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01U5)

proof.text: *Condition (3), the base change of an affine open.* Keep the notation of step 3 and let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-scheme]; then $f|_U:U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\alpha$ for a unique ring map $\alpha:R\to A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], making $A$ an $R$-algebra. Let $U'=g'^{-1}(U)$, an open subscheme of $X'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] (applied to $g'$ and $U$) the square formed by $U'\to U$, $U'\hookrightarrow X'$, $U\hookrightarrow X$, $g'$ is cartesian; it sits on top of the cartesian square $(X',g',f')$ of $f$ and $g$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the outer rectangle is cartesian: $U'$ with $U'\to U$ and $f'|_{U'}:U'\to S'$ is a fibre product $U\times_SS'$ of $f|_U$ and $g$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism, there is an isomorphism $U'\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RR')$ under which $f'|_{U'}$ becomes $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $R'\to A\otimes_RR'$, $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$. In particular $U'$ is an affine open of $X'$ with $f'(U')\subseteq S'$, $S'$ affine, and the ring map $\mathcal O_{S'}(S')=R'\to\mathcal O_{X'}(U')\cong A\otimes_RR'$ induced by $f'$ is $r'\mapsto1\otimes r'$. Since $f'$ is locally of finite type, this ring map is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] (with $U'\subseteq X'$, $V=S'$). Through the swap isomorphism $A\otimes_RR'\cong R'\otimes_RA$, $a\otimes r'\mapsto r'\otimes a$, which is an isomorphism of $R'$-algebras (it carries generators to generators), this says: $A'=R'\otimes_RA$, with $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$, is a finite type $R'$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KX, proof: 'Let U ⊂ X be an affine open. Then U' = S' ×_S U is affine and of finite type over S' ... U = Spec(A), U' = Spec(A') ... A' = R' ⊗_R A and R' -> A' is of finite type' (Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01T2 (1)=>(2) for the last clause)

proof.text: *Condition (3), conclusion.* By step 3, $\rho:R\to R'$ is faithfully flat, and by step 4, $R'\otimes_RA$ is a finite type $R'$-algebra; so $\alpha:R\to A$ is of finite type by the direction 'if' of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-descends-faithfully-flat]. The ring map $\alpha$ is the map $\mathcal O_S(S)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$ induced by $f$, with $U\subseteq X$ and $S$ affine opens and $f(U)\subseteq S$. Every $x\in X$ lies in an affine open $U$ [def-pc-scheme], so the criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] holds at every point (with $V=S$), and $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus being locally of finite type satisfies condition (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion].

source.place: Descent, Lemma Tag 02KX, proof: 'We have to show that R -> A is of finite type. This is the result of Algebra, Lemma 00QP (lemma-finite-type-descends, algebra.tex line 31443). It follows that f is locally of finite type.'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 1, 2 and 5 the class of morphisms locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] satisfies conditions (0)-(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-local-on-base-criterion]. Applied to $f:X\to S$ and the fpqc covering $\{g_i:S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering], whose base changes $f_i:X\times_SS_i\to S_i$ are locally of finite type by hypothesis, it gives that $f$ is locally of finite type.
